root_cause.verdict: No connection reuse + per-connection mbedTLS handshake cost: every media.cnn.com image opens a NEW TCP+TLS connection (CurlShareHandle shares COOKIE/DNS/SSL_SESSION but NOT CURL_LOCK_DATA_CONNECT) and each TLS handshake on the loaded single-vCPU TCG windowed guest takes ~29s wall time (tcpdump: wire clean, server 15-50ms; 13-32s gaps are guest-side, not loss). The 31s/63s 'RTO-looking' modals are handshake-compute starvation, not RTO backoff.
evidence: Windowed 701: images nconn=1 every fetch, tls median 29033ms/total 29289ms max 50129ms; fonts to same IP 2.3s -> cost is per-connection TLS setup
Headless 60x same kernel/binary/URLs/edges: tls median 232ms total 264ms -> network path not slow
Windowed 705 + CURL_LOCK_DATA_CONNECT: 116 images, 115 reused nconn=0, tls median 0ms total median 134ms -> reuse collapses stall
tcpdump eth0 to Fastly: zero data retransmits; two guest-silence gaps (13.3s pre-ClientHello, 32.1s pre-Finished) = guest CPU
resolv.c emits QTYPE A only -> no AAAA ever (H2 refuted in source)
entropy is non-blocking xorshift+CNTPCT (H4 refuted by code)
run 700 full log: 126 fetches, image mean 48.8s, one handshake per fetch

measurements.note: -smp2 no help; guest single-core (PSCI power-on fails)

patches.what: CurlShareHandle CONNECT-sharing: curl_share_setopt(CURLSHOPT_SHARE, CURL_LOCK_DATA_CONNECT) + connectMutex in mutexFor
patches.expected: image total median 29289ms -> 134ms; nconn 1->0 after first per-host fetch; ~97-image CNN wave ~47min->~30s

patches.what: Async/pooled subresource fetches (fetch off the parser thread)
patches.expected: removes parser blocking + ~26s one-time handshake per host under load

patches.what: HTTP/2 multiplexing over the shared connection
patches.expected: one TLS conn + multiplexed image streams (probe shows hv=2 available)
no stall effect; H2/H3 not the cause

os_diff_proposal: No OS-side change needed for the 97-image stall (headless same stack = 230ms). Optional OS lever: fix PSCI secondary-core power-on under TCG (currently 'Failed to power-on core N') to give the guest a real 2nd vCPU and cut the ~26s one-time handshake contention.
